newsitem.title: UK: WORLD LPG FIRMER DESPITE SLACK SUMMER INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: WORLD LPG FIRMER DESPITE SLACK SUMMER INTEREST.

text.p: International liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices were mostly firmer this week despite fairly lacklustre summer buying interest.
In Europe, a large propane cargo was heard sold at $195 a tonne cif NWE on Thursday, $5 up on last week's traded levels. Prices were still pegged in the mid $190s on Friday.
The coaster market was also a shade firmer with deals heard at $187.75 and $190 fob UK.
"There's not much material available on the coaster marker, but then there's not any significant demand either," said one trader.
Despite unenthusiastic demand, a slow down in throughput at Norway's Karsto terminal was lending support to the market, dealers said.
Maintenance at Norway's giant Sleipner gas field, which supplies Karsto, was scheduled for August 7-19 and expected to reduce LPG output by around 30 percent.

Butane cargoes were traded earlier in the week on a fob basis in the high $150s and low $160s, although buyers looked scarce later in the week. Cif cargoes were valued higher at about 90 percent of naphtha prices, or around $175 a tonne.
In the Mediterranean, healthy petrochemical demand underpinned prices for butane, but trade was slow.
A similar story was reported in the Far East although the year's lowest Saudi contract price (CP) was encouraging buyers to try and push back September loadings and buy on the spot market.
"People are trying to take advantage of the low prices now and build up stocks for winter, although there have hardly been any firm deals," said one trader.
Differentials to the CP firmed slightly, implying the market has bottomed out.
"If buyers think the September CP is going to be higher they'll want to buy now," a trader said.
In Japan, propane was assessed at a premium of $16-$20 to the CP on a c+f basis. Gulf fob cargoes were pegged firmer at CP -$5/-$2 for butane and -$6/-$3 for propane.
Two propane cargoes traded on an fob basis earlier in the week at August CP -$8 and -$7 respectively.
In the United States, prices firmed over the course of the week, despite the release of bearish stocks data.

Propane reached around 36.50 cents a gallon at the Mont Belvieu, Texas trading hub although Wednesday's Energy Information Administration data showed July inventories increased by 7.1 million barrels.
Some players suggested that speculation by large trading companies was driving the market higher in the face of bearish fundamentals.
